notes.title: The World and Gameplay Update
notes.notes:
Greetings fellow Dwarves! Today we are super excited to announce Orebound's latest update: The World and Gameplay Update.



This is a very large, exciting update that has improved many aspects of the game. There's multiple changes coming in this new update that improve multiple systems inside the game. We will write a full detailed description of what's been changed, but below is a nice summary:

 
[olist]
A new dynamic material system for the entire game that vastly improves how the world renders. 

Multiple Biome overhauls, new snow forest, new jungle, new woodlands, new materials for rocks and trees. 

Major lighting changes, caves are now much darker but lights have been boosted massively to light up underground. Night lighting has also been overhauled. 

Minecart systems overhaul. Huge changes here, mine carts can now be put into groups, filtered and split or merged. 

Market improvements. The market now provides every item to purchase in the game as you unlock them. Also a brand new model. 

NPC head tracking system. 

An additional 9 minute sound track. 

Refreshed main menu. 

Lore in the citadel to read. 

Hunger Re-balance 

Notification Improvements  
[/olist]


With the changes made in this update, we hope both returning and new players will be able to enjoy the new views as they climb the tallest peaks, or explore to the darkest depths!



If you love Orebound and want to share your ideas, builds or feature requests, join our Discord server here: https://discord.gg/tRt7KDak

  
Landscape Material System Overhaul 
Behind the scenes, we've been working hard to ensure the world of Orebound is immersive and exciting to play. One way we have improved the landscape is through new triplanar technique upgrades. These changes help make the landscape more varied and appealing while traversing the world. 




Previously, our smaller-scale materials system worked decently for the first few updates of the game, but as we continue to build upon the expansive world of Orebound, we needed a stronger and improved system for our materials. One of the biggest issues we have with Orebound is getting a complex procedurally generated landscape to texture properly with multiple layers and multiple depths or angles.



We worked tirelessly to create our new system that not only has improved graphics for current biomes, but will also allow us to create more distinct cave layers and biomes in the future. Our new system uses pretty complex math to determine which material should be shown, which helps bring more depth and structure to the environment around you, particularly for mountains and cave entrances.  You’ll start to see more improvements in the future for below ground now that our environment generation is maturing into a much nicer state. 



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/993f70e79b211a74737c2be95b3a9d77105abf49.png"]

Environment Improvements - Biome Overhauls
We have continued our efforts from previous updates to improve the environment presented in the Orebound by improving individual biomes. For some time, most of the biomes did not feel completely unique, which took away from the overall experience. Most biomes have seen both material and item additions. For example, snow mountains and snow areas have been overhauled and divided into two biomes and the mountains are now split between lower and upper. Each of which now contain their own models and details. 

 

Snow forests have also been improved, with new snow pine trees, snowy grass and new material outlines, making traversing the snowy lands more exciting for players visually.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/ac9542ed0f197ec1ee73b75ea8e935d402502854.png"]

The rocky biome now has different rocks to make the biome more unique, including bigger boulders which may take longer to destroy, but give a high stone return.




The Jungle has now been completely redesigned with new plants and consumables and looks vastly better than before. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/23204e41619b40e7408f1514c273837057c451b9.jpg"]

These changes mean that not only will the world be more immersive for new or returning players, but will allow for more distinct biomes to be added in the future.


Lighting

One major change we have made is the lighting in the caves. We became aware of how bright the caves previously were, which took away the mystery or the adventurous elements of looking for precious ores, and made the torches redundant. Many players asked for the caves to be darker and on our playtests we actually really enjoy playing this way.  



We have adjusted the caves’ lighting to make the experience more realistic, by decreasing the brightness of the caves. This now means that torches are now essential when diving deeper into the mines as you may not be able to see what lies ahead.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/e53f056498703438575b4ea474f22aec92f43b6b.png"]We have increased the lighting power of all lights so people have plenty of light range whilst exploring the dark. All in all they just needed a lot of balance to get the dark/light gameplay correct. 


However, they are too bright for most base building uses so to counter this we have given players the ability to turn lights up or down in intensity. So now you can change the brightness of your base lights to match!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/0b8c2471027cc0d0a12d0326ff7e74a26990023b.png"]

We will likely tweak these values later on depending on player feedback but we’re happy with the changes for now!


Minecarts
Our previous minecart system did not have a lot of complex capabilities, which made organising tracks and stations difficult for players. As we recognised that minecarts have not had a fresh overhaul, we have now finished a new experimental mincart system with new UI, but also focused on how players can use them effectively in their builds. 

 

In order to help organise minecart systems, we have introduced minecart grouping, which allows players to select stations, minecarts and rail splitters to group together so they only interact with each other. This means that if there’s several stations on the same rail line, but not all are a part of the group, then the minecart will not interact with the groupless stations and will skip to the next grouped station.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/9006e0d85525936253fa4f14905fcf8e9e522fcc.png"]

Two new types of rails have also been introduced to allow for more complex rail systems: the Rail Splitter and the Rail Merger. Rail Splitters have the ability to filter one side by a specific Minecart Group which allows the player to split routes and send specific carts to different areas or stations, and then after use Rail Mergers to merge back into the main route. Rail Splitters with no group will split Minecarts 50/50.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/1246a864d04958179f69f178b8676572fea8eac3.png"]

Minecarts themselves now have two inventory slots instead of one, helping speed up the process of transferring goods from different stations. Minecarts don't require space to drop their entire content anymore, they'll drop whatever the station can store, and will no longer stop at full stations.


Market Rework
The needed market changes overhaul is here! Markets now sell a larger array of useful items (now priced higher than their actual value, he’s got to make his market profitable somehow!) that previously were not purchasable, making more items accessible to players. Items can also be bought in bulk, up to the maximum item stack size, which saves a significant amount of time for players who previously had to manually purchase individual items. New items are also unlocked by upgrading your research level, giving players even more reasons to regularly check their research stations to see what they need to reach the next level. This also comes with a new model as the old one didn't quite fit. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/b8ab5b336815e99524d807c6dd56f72c9728f5b7.png"]

NPC Head Tracking
This one is smaller but still vital, all NPCs, including orcs, will now track the player with their heads. This was something we wanted to get to earlier but other tasks took priority. In addition all Dwarven NPC’s have been made more unique and individual. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/264f91c6913fca89459dcb4e054c63ea97c68cfa.png"]

  Update notes:

New triplanar calculation and optimisations, allowing new landscape material.  We've added a lot here, including different top and side material display, and near and far textures with blending between them.

Changed the navigator behavior so that it only drains mana when moving. Mana will regen when you stay stationary

When you obtain a Tool and there is free space in your Hotbar it'll automatically set it to that slot

Moved general notifications to the center of the screen

Added more notifications for the building tool modes

Details on landscape biome changes:

The jungle biome has been changed in style to a different type of forest.  The jungle was using market place assets and the new assets are custom creations by our artist dwarf.

The snow forest biome has been redone, with new material outline, snow grass and snow pine trees.

The mountains are now actual mountains, not just snow and are split into two new biomes, the lower mountain and upper mountain.  The upper mountain goes all the way through, the lower mountain has just a hard outer stone shell and dirt inside.  Mining the stone parts of the lower and upper mountain requires a level 2 pickaxe and will give you stone.

The desert biome, while still barren, now looks more sandy.

The rocky biome now has different rocks, including large boulders that will take a lot to destroy and will give a larger stone reward.

Changed the navigator behavior so that it only drains mana when moving. Mana will regenerate when you stay stationary

When you obtain a Tool and there is free space in your Hotbar it'll automatically set it to that slot

Moved general notifications to the center of the screen

Added more notifications for the building tool modes

Minecart System Improvements:

Minecarts will now take items from the last slots and not the first.

Minecarts now have 2 inventory slots instead of 1 which helps with item flow and stations that contain different types of items.

Minecarts don't require space to drop their entire content anymore, they'll drop whatever the station can store.

Minecarts that can't deposit items or can't pick items up won't do a full stop at the station anymore

Fixes to the station and cart collisions and rail heights.

Minecart Groups System

The addition of Minecart Groups which is a system that will allow players to create and assign groups to Minecart Stations, Minecarts and Rail Splitters. The groups system will allow players more control and automation of their Rail Networks.

A minecart will only perform a stop and interact with a station if they are of the same group, it will totally skip stations assigned to other groups than itself. This allows players to control which carts can interact with which stations and thus control the flow of items by controlling the number of carts available to each station of a certain Group.

A minecart can be interacted with to see its contents and to change its group after it has been created.

The addition of Rail Splitters and Rail Mergers to allow for more complex Rail Networks.

Rail Splitters have the ability to filter one side by a specific Minecart Group which allows the player to split routes and send specific carts to different areas or stations and then after use Rail Mergers to merge back into the main route.

Rail Splitters with no group will split Minecarts 50/50

Changed lighting values for all light based buildings in the build hammer to suit the new overall cave lighting changes

New icons for buildings within the first page of the build hammer

"Dwarfified" some in game text

Tweaked a couple of food recipes - boar bacon sandwich, barley bread.

Added new items into the jungle- Blue Jungle shroom & Jungle bush

Dwarves are now interactable within the citadel and will have unique text.

Market Rework:

Market now sells new Items

New items are unlocked through research

Buying items from Market costs more than their actual value

Can select any amount of an item to buy between 1 and the max stack size

Improved NPC Visuals:

Most NPCs now look at the player when they get near, or are being targeted in the case of orcs

Blacksmith dwarf now only hammers when crafting

Market dwarf now only waves when  you interact with him (Open or close shop)

Bug Fixes:

Build mode switch sound now gets effected by SFX volume setting

Fixed clicking around Tutorial popup sometimes hiding mouse (Also takes away player movement until dismissed)

Hunger only damages the player to a certain amount

Peaceful and Easy only damages the player to 50 health

Standard only damages the player to 10 health

Hard only damages the player to 1 health

Very Hard will reduce health to 0 and kill the player

We also might be working on something special for Orebound’s 1 Year Anniversary, so stay tuned ;)

notes.title: The Outpost Update
notes.notes:
Fellow Dwarves, we are excited to announce a smaller, but significant update: The Outpost Update.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/348372acb3b71979d7d990726e44751e34874695.png"]
The Outpost Update
The main focus of this update is improving the game’s performance so more players can have higher frames per second. This means more players should have a seamless experience while exploring the world of Orebound. We've achieved this through using imposters on Unreal Engine to reduce the amount of graphics your PC will have to render at a distance, without losing the quality Orebound is known for.




To help improve performance, we also identified areas that were being rendered when they shouldn’t be. This has made massive savings, from an average of 7 million triangles rendered down to, in some places, under 1 million triangles. For our test machines, we've seen increases between 10-20 fps, and we hope for lower end machines this should be greater.  We've taken the liberty of using some of this freed up space to increase the foliage. The pine forest is now denser and renders out further, and the grass is now thicker.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/017be2125c00961e69ff1b6362c3d30be4246b16.png"]



A New Way To Build
A highly requested feature we are excited to finally introduce is drag lines for building. Placing individual building pieces takes a while, so the use of our new drag features to help speed up the process of building your base, giving you more time to fully explore your world. Most building pieces can be drag-placed horizontally or vertically, with the exception being stairs, which can be placed diagonally.



Full Quest Rework
As a part of our mission to make the gameplay experience the most enjoyable as we can. The tutorial has been disabled and the onboarding process has seen a full and lengthy rework to replace it. The early gameplay flow is now far, far smoother and more satisfying to play.

Quests will now automatically track and complete for the player, requirements and rewards will display in the quest HUD, and the onboarding has been redesigned to fit around the new Dwarven Outpost building, your centralised point for all expeditions! 


Citadel Improvements
We have also been working behind the scenes on improving the Citadel and the overall onboarding process for new players. The Citadel now contains new carpets to help direct players, improved lighting to make the Citadel more lively, and new relay stations.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/07b5950a3f3dcab489a3956e9e6528a250f0c4e4.png"]
New Building!
We are excited to announce a new building to the game: The Outpost - a central starting base camp on your dwarven adventure. The Outpost is a perfect starting base, whether you are new to the game or travelled far from your original spawn. A bed, King’s Quest Board and a chest can all be found in the outpost, making it the ideal first build you make.



Mountains!
There is also a change to the generator for the surface.  Mountain generation has been reconfigured.  No more random seeds where mountains take up most of the map and you’re stuck on a desolate peak, desperately searching for berries and mushrooms to stave off hunger.  Instead we’ve toned down how much space a mountain takes up, while bringing them closer together.  The result is a mix of valleys and plains along with ridges and ranges to construct your dwarven fortresses in.  The extra benefit is the land is a bit more bumpy, and endless flat prairies have been broken up.



To see some of the new update in action, check out our trailer for The Outpost Update here: [dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/n5i2ifl-oow"][/dynamiclink]



Future Plans…?
And now fellow dwarves, as if this update wasn't enough, more food for ye eyes to make your stomachs grumble in hunger and whet your appetite for our future plans.  These will not necessarily arrive in order, but plans they are.




1) Forging your own image.

This one in particular we wanted done for this patch, but timing and resources be as they are, it is delayed. The back end continues for the character creator for you sculpt your jaw, choose your braids, colour your eyes like gems and rock.  Also introducing a new feature we're calling "the trait system".  But more on that will be revealed, later.




2) The landscape shall bloom anew!

Many have remarked the world is pretty and good, and the style unique, and aye, we have gone for style.  Though during our changes and musings, we want to make more.  Edges on far away hills and cliffs should reveal uncovered ground and sides, and the realm should pop.  The mountains will call to ye, lusting to be mined.




3) Glory of the new outposts.

The new dwarven outpost was created by chief engineers, combining stone and wood, with fresh dwarven designs and we know, you want those pieces to incorporate into your dwarven holds.  Our plan for that involves a menu recategorization.  No more rummaging through lists of stone and wood building chaos like a drunk goblin in a gear bin.  We plan to make it that ye shall find pieces laid out neat as a master masons toolkit!




4) Weaving of the world

With the changing of the maps so that the mountains no longer dominate (not that any dwarf is not home within their sacred mountain halls) and vast planes do not stretch for miles beyond, we plan to expose these parameters in your selection, to edit and play with so you can get a world you want to enjoy!  Create realms as unique as the self carves runes on ye axe!  And of course, with this will come a visualizer, so you can see what surface you'll adventure onto.  Of course though, the deep bowels will remain a mystery you have to explore yerself





Patch Notes:

Generation has been changed for mountains, they take up less room and are more frequent, making the world bumpier.  This only applies in new games.

New axe model and animation for wood chopping axe

All foliage and camp items have imposters, which are light weight triangle representations when they are far away.

The lorestone at game start finds the ground better.

Finding the start area now has a stronger bias for flat zones (should stop starting up sheer cliffs)

New Rune Line drag system, to drag place buildings.  The default hotkey is M.

On player death,if you are in build mode, this will now cancel.

Optimized skeletons using animation budgeting in citadel

The foot IK is now off while in the airship (should stop your feet going in the air while the airship is moving)

Doubled the distance for placing buildings in build mode from 20m to 40m

Can no longer use tools while in a building's UI

Can no longer scroll through hotbar while in a building's UI

Player Inventory should now close along with building UI

Can no longer search for king's quest board with beacon compass

Added New Dwarven Outpost building

Can now use beacon compass to search for Outpost

Added a Barkeep to Citadel who gives out drinks

Quest and game balance changes

Completely disabled the tutorial 

Fully reworked the onboarding process to be more guided 

Quests will now automatically complete once fulfilled 

Added the Dwarven outpost, a new base of operations for the player 

Reworked the costs of the Toolsmith, bed and King’s Questboard

Rewritten the lore on the starting Lorestone 

Added more relay beacons to the citadel

Added carpets to help navigate the citadel 

Changed the default FOV from 90-100

You can now get drunk at the citadel Anvil bar!

notes.title: Orebound - Anvil Update 2: Multiplayer
notes.notes:
Fellow Dwarves, bring your clan to diggy hole together in Anvil Update 2: Multiplayer. 



The long-anticipated multiplayer update is here! We heard you loud and clear, and we’re excited for you and your friends to explore the world of Orebound together. After months of hard-work and dedication, we can’t wait for you to try the new version of the game. 



Currently, the multiplayer update is available for beta testers, but will be available to the public on Saturday 21st June 2025. Anyone who would like to get access to it early can use the code updatenow321.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/d00f94049086535280c5959ed9395cc26eef3109.png"]


Orebound Multiplayer Capabilities
Currently, up to 5 players are supported, allowing you and four friends to mine, go caving and build your automations. 



Up to 10 players can play, however, this is currently experimental and will become fully supported in the future. Play at your own risk.



Play with either your Steam friends, or join public servers to help dwarves across the globe build a mining empire. Use custom settings to help shape your multiplayer experience.

 

Whether you decide to all work together on the same quest, or work on individual ones, different clan members can track different quests to help build your mining factory faster. Alternatively, if you fancy making the game harder, you can also disable the quest user interface in the settings to really test your knowledge of the game.



Multiplayer notifications have also been implemented, meaning you can bully your clan members when they die for a dumb reason 😉


In-Game Tweaks
On top of releasing multiplayer, we also took the time to amend different in-game UI and quality of life changes to help make the game more streamlined and easier to access. 


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/00db5aa2deee50ffc1fc8373b578cbf0fb4b67e2.png"]
Better Balanced Quests and Rewards
One of the most significant changes to the game is the rebalancing of quests to make them more achievable, and to give better quests rewards. This will help encourage natural progression in the game.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/b96fb82c58f77902ff5be9648dabde89db281b88.png"]
New UX For Main Menu
We have decided to update and improve the user interface for the main menu to help streamline the game for all users. This means that 


The Navigator - New UX Overhaul
The Navigator has also had an upgrade, which now shows improved outlines for all minable ores, making it easier to find the right ores. However, using the Navigator and the Compass now use mana, so you’ll have to be mindful of how you use these items!


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/1746bd7db3f0515f2e3ab9102ab0a58cc559cf52.png"]
Citadel Changes
To make the citadel more accessible and easier to explore, new carpets and signs have been added to help guide new players. There is also new added lore to the citadel - we hope you enjoy learning more about the world of Orebound!



In the near future, we will be continuing development to the Citadel to support multiplayer and to make it a stronger hub world. Stay tuned!


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/de782a63ed6c26901e1bea7107bd904b10d8f4c0.png"]
Graphics Improvements
We have also reworked some of the graphics for the main menu, smelter, build menu, blacksmith, and quest menu to help them stand out more.

notes.title: The Next Update Branch - Experimental Multiplayer Update
notes.notes:
My fellow Dwarves, we have been silent toiling deep in the research centres and alchemists halls (coding non stop) and finally, it's been requested and we've been hounded for this since day one, but it is here!

And we are happy to save that we are pushing now to TheNextUpdate branch the coming Anvil update 2, the multiplayer update!  With it, as well as getting multiplayer support fully working, comes several other changes.

The multipalyer menu can be found inside the Citadel relay, where there is a new multiplayer option, where you can choose to host a new game or load up an existing game!

Yes that is right, all your current old games should be multiplayer ready.  However we highly advise before you invite someone to your already created Dwarven stronghold you first load up the game, save the game on a new save, and use this new save for your multiplayer.

A note, you have to load up multiplayer game from inside the citadel relay multiplayer menu.  If you try load up a game from multiplayer from inside an already multiplayer game, it'll turn to singple player.

We have plans for the future, including seeing your friends inside the Citadel where you can meet up.  More to be expanded on at a later time.

Alongside multiplayer are some optimizations, some fixes and rebalancing to the Kings quest board to improve the Dwarven experience.

So go fourth, dig for the King, expand the Dwarven lands, and claim the three gems!

Dig deep and hold!

Features

- Maximum of 10 players

Quests

- The quest tracking now can be tracked via group, which is controlled by the host.  There is option in the settings to turn this off.

- The Finest dwarven lumbar quest reward will give a navigator and gold to all joined players

- New quests in the Kings Quest board to complete!

- The blow them up quest has a reward reduction.

- All other quests have a reward improvement

- All quests in the construction section have seen their requirements halved.

World

- Tunnel orcs have been re-added.  They will now spawn if they are too near a base.  But expect sometimes they'll move around and get curious.

Buildings

- Machines now show how many items they need and make a minute.

- Citadel relay options have new UI.

- Multiplayer option added to citadel relay.

- The build menu has been updated with UI changes.

Misc

- The navigators are changed and all shows ores in the world, their different is their range.  Their old functionality still works though.

- Inside of the settings menu there is a resync button for multiplayer for clients to resync their voxel world if they find things are not lining up properly.

- A multiplayer list to show the connected players in your game.  By default the hotbar is p.

- The mining helmet has been given a nice little candle flame when it is turned on.

- An alert will appear when a player dies and when a player kills another player.

- Different way of loading up the voxel world edits.  Should be faster now.

- The camera height has been shifted up slightly so you actually look other dwarves in the eye now, instead of the nose being at camera height.

- Location of Ore navigator in tool station is closer to the top of the menu.

notes.notes:
Fellow dwarves!{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png

Grab your hammers and tighten those toolbelts — the Frameforge Update is here, and it brings with it the biggest overhaul to building Orebound has ever seen. After weeks of mining through feedback, hammering out bugs, and chiseling in improvements, we've crafted a building system worthy of your mighty underground empires.

 🧱The Way We Build Has Changed🧱
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
Let’s start with the big one: the introduction of Frameforge Mode — a brand new, grid-aligned building mode that makes snapping pieces into place faster, cleaner, and more intuitive than ever before.

Whether you're assembling a humble smelting hut or a sprawling industrial complex, Frameforge Mode helps keep everything perfectly aligned across long distances, even when building at angles. For those who prefer a bit more creative chaos, Freeplace Mode remains — letting you plonk and rotate to your heart’s content, grid-free.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/11158b507ec4aa55f489cc215791c0b255efe5b9.jpg

We’ve also simplified the system from three build modes down to two. Why? Because dwarves like things clear and practical. Now, every dwarf knows exactly which tool to use and when.

📐Precision with a Global Grid📐
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png

We’ve swapped the old system for a fully global grid, ensuring that your factory lines, conveyor chains, and towering constructs all line up cleanly, no matter how deep or wide your plans go. This change alone eliminates tons of small frustrations and makes Orebound’s world feel far more consistent.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/be72d90d2378062a908de20d1b4c3459e75377bf.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/bbb0ad6a2a3234e894d3347e6a0c8ac9abc9f327.jpg

Even better, you can now choose your grid size — whether you're working on detailed inner workings or laying out huge structural frames, the grid works the way you want it to.

🔩Snaps That Make More Sense🔩
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
Let’s talk snap points. We heard your beard-scratching confusion loud and clear — certain pieces just weren’t snapping the way they should, and larger structures felt like they were ignoring the rules entirely. That’s fixed.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/97d13acd2d9e302429760137980bcecae438fbdd.jpg

We’ve massively expanded and refined the snap point system, especially for large and extra-large pieces. Now, pieces snap exactly where you expect them to — top, bottom, sides — it all just works. You’ll even find tile snaps on the tops of foundations (yes, even the XL ones), and new bottom snaps to help with stacking.

And in response to one of the most common feature requests from you clever cave-dwellers — stone and wood pieces are now fully intercompatible. That’s right: you can now seamlessly mix and match stone and wood building components without awkward snap rejections or clunky transitions. Build with style and substance!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/a9d66a239dc0a109d959403f2813fdf3d07c8e74.jpg

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/b7d8f1c2ba83b56b8b0c282e2615a1beb7d71e7a.jpg


 🧹Smoothing Out the Cracks🧹
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
This update also crushes a whole heap of bugs and annoyances that were getting in the way of your creative flow:

🛠 Frameforge Update – Full Patch Notes🛠 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png

🌐 Core Building System Changes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
 Changed colour of snap points from mint green to a calmer green.
 Reduced snap point size by 30%.
 Reduced snap point glow intensity by 50%.
 All machines now snap on the top of wood and stone block types: stone foundation, wood large foundation, large stone foundation, and XL wood foundations.
 Stone and wood building pieces are now fully intercompatible.
 Machines now use the global grid system in smart plan mode — individual machine snap points removed.
 Snap point size and glow reduced further for clarity.
 Snap point visibility can now be toggled in settings.
 Edge snapping for square and tile pieces is now 50% closer to the edges.
 Pivot points of several machines have been adjusted to better align with grid placement in smart plan mode. Note: some belts may need to be replaced to align correctly.
 Snap points now invalidate if a dwarf is standing where the building would be placed.
 Buildings can no longer be placed on top of yourself — no more accidental self-entombment.
 Chains can now be rotated in all directions.
 Snap points that share the same location now only show the first valid one, reducing clutter and visual bloom.

🧱 Snap Fixes and Additions
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
 Fixed top-of-ladder snaps.
 Large wooden pillars now snap properly under foundations and large wood foundations.
 Elevator snaps improved.
 Lights on chains now snap correctly when placed.
 Snap points added to both ends of chains.
 Small coin storage snap points fixed.
 Snap for gate corners on square piece types corrected.
 Small and large tile snaps now work on wood wall pieces.
 Belt stands now snap to each other.
 Wall torch lights now use grid size 1 to fix bad rotation in forge frame mode.
 Wood walls and wide wood walls now snap properly to stone foundation, large wood, large stone, and XL wood foundations.
 Large foundation snaps added to top corners of wood foundation and stone wall square pieces — now function like multiple stone foundation pieces combined.
 Elevator sides and tops now support snaps for square and tile pieces.
 Fixed splitters, mergers, and ammo splitter snaps not working.
 All top snaps that accept square building pieces now also accept ladders.
 Increased foundation bottom snap radius by 20%.
 Added missing snaps to foundation and large wood tile pieces.
 Fixed wood wall snapping too low on wood tile/stone slabs.
 Fixed wood railing missing top snap.
 Increased detection radius of side square pieces by 10%.
 Wall torch pivot points now set to the bottom of the mesh, consistent with braziers.

🏗️ General Building Improvements
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
 Deposits should no longer spawn in camps in new games. In existing saves, deposit locations are fixed.
 Fixed a reload issue with blacksmiths not accepting coins anymore.
 Pipes now display arrow directions during placement mode.
 Fixed tools not playing their animation properly when switching.
 Fixed ladder jumping issue when placed over the player.
 Fixed small brazier having collision when placing.
 Removed problematic brazier collision that launched players while placing
 Fixed snap points not reappearing when switching between build modes.
 Buildings now place over the player without pushing you around.
 Large stone foundation pieces now appear at the top of the stone section for easier access.
 King’s Market pivot point centered — may require rebuilding if previously offset.
 You can no longer take food from spit if your inventory is full.
 Many guideline snap positions have been adjusted to sit at the bottom of the structure.

🛡️Combat, AI, and Game World Fixes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
 AI now falls significantly faster when in freefall.
 Boars no longer appear from thin air — but you might still spot them rustling through the undergrowth.
 Fixed walking and sprinting animation bugs.
 Fixed dead enemies falling through the floor a few seconds after dying.
 Fixed explosives not causing damage.
 Improved spawn detection so boars don’t stop spawning near large bases.
 Fixed deposits spawning inside orc camps and POIs (new games only).
 Barricades in orc camps now display correct names instead of showing as flags.
 Fixed Navigator occasionally not working.
 Fixed double damage sometimes being applied to weapons.
 Fixed double damage when weapons were unequipped while selected.
 Fixed missing weapon damage on game load when in first inventory slot.
 Chest closing sounds now respect the audio slider.
 Fixed not receiving the Steam reward for completing “The Beginning” questline.

✈️ Airship and Citadel Changes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
 When pressing “Go to Airship,” lights now flash around the ship and propellers spin at half speed to signal readiness.
 Fixed a bug where you could launch yourself out of the airship while climbing the left turret at game start.

🧰 Blacksmiths and Crafting
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
 Fixed blacksmiths not auto-starting crafting with “refill recipe” (still requires gold input manually).
 Removed spam from “refill recipe” and “take all” messages when interacting with manual buildings.

Dwarven Community Highlights! 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
We also wanted to share with you some amazing worlds our community have been creating over the last few months! 

Desorniph's Fortress
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/02001e82acbb61ca91c1b7f0bb6de61d485feef6.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/db18544fd796e1ce4e9b3858682c0a17d7be0bac.jpg


Awesomekeksi's Megafort
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/ff2c311370697c53024a2cb83faafe45e1b84e35.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/b1169919d6dee2456c92a7a2e8216d8691db3024.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/18c4d474f6840155c83795ff6cbea5f66f84626f.jpg

Next week, we’ll be making a massive announcement about the next update.


If you're enjoying the game, we'd really appreciate if you dropped a review to help us out! Until then, keep building, keep sharing, and keep digging deeper.
— The Dwarven Devs

notes.title: ANVIL UPDATE 1
notes.notes:
ANVIL UPDATE 1 PREVIEW

Fellow Dwarves! Welcome to Anvil Update 1. 

This update is one of the biggest yet for the game. Today we celebrate Anvil Update 1s Early… Early Access? With an epic insight into the research and development of our Dwarves. Please Enjoy and share the video with your Dwarven friends! 

[previewyoutube=ey-vTveUXJ8;full][/previewyoutube]

We will be setting this to “thenextupdate” branch of Orebound.  It is VERY experimental, but we have decided it's time to show everyone what we’ve been working on for the last few months. We have been hitting the anvil super hard. Seriously, we've been working flat out on this update... 

This can be accessed in the game properties on Steam with 

password : updatenow321 

A big thank you to all our fellow Dwarven Supporters! Please drop us a review if you're enjoying the game! 

Multiple Major Feature Additions

Stackable Belts & Stackable Pipes 
This update introduces the ability to perfectly stack belts and pipes onto each other. It’s been one of the most heavily requested features since launch and today we are delivering that in Anvil Update 1. They are awesome. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/1bddde1d1847f330a7a5b1e3fba156fef1f18795.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/616db378cc559ab00dc3c7cc1b563e36ec64b284.png

Straight Mode & Automatic Angles for belts
We have implemented the ability to have perfectly straight belts and also added the ability to do perfect right angles on demand with the system. This will now allow players to make epicly neat factories! We also added the ability to hold CTRL to lock belts to a straight line. These also apply to Pipes and Rails.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/8ba3a837faf508ac2eebb3f823c2b9fb8bf9588e.png

New Splitters and Mergers
Orebound now has 2 new splitters and mergers ( both are three way splits and merges ) that also stack onto each other so they should also fit with the stackable belts in perfect harmony. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/d213aeda72287ace9fe997b33dbafd363da02d61.png

New Inputs and outputs for machines
The game now has completely overhauled input and output for machines, allowing a consistent height for all machines, we also added input and output signs for each machine to make it clearer where items go in and out. 

Warning - Belts on old saves will look misaligned but will still function correctly. If you want to fix the visual you'll need to rebuild them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/054997126f8c0613ca5b39bfa79a80fa1b165947.png

Vertical Belts
Today we are adding vertical belts so players can send items directly 90 up and 90 down. These work much like other vertical belts we’re sure you’ve experienced before.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/6db011bd6817801c9289e3a4358357f0169c7dd5.png

Additional Base Building Pieces
We have added over 10  new pieces to the game to make bases with. They include large platforms and more stone pieces to make interesting bases. We noticed it was taking ages to make large bases, even just to place platforms. So we have added much larger ones to save time. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/7ffed292452fc3a1132371cb54955b5fa4b3d59c.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/ee7a06835c3f0aaeba17e2705d4f3c5d4ec55278.png

Optimizations of the saving and loading systems
Players will notice saving and loading times being way faster after making a new save post-update. The save sizes also will see a big reduction up to x10 times smaller.


Major Reworks to the building system. 

The building snap system has been remade from the ground up.  It has been changed to a data on demand system instead of a constant existing system.  

This may not visibly look like a major change but we have had to completely rewrite this building system therefore there's likely to be issues here for a short time whilst we fix it up!

We figured out that for some buildings, they contributed between 200-700 uobjects, which was causing the crash and vastly increasing gameplay loading times. The limit as some of you have found is 2 million. 

This system now greatly reduces that number, improving performance from unnecessary overhead and banishing the uobject crash until you get a mega fortress running (we'll come up with ways to deal with that later).

The snap system now displays new snap indicators so you can see where to place your buildings much better than the tiny dots we had before.  We are hoping to continue improving this system in the future.

The snap system has now expanded and centralised many buildings offsets and rotations for easy snap sharing.  Yes, that means many buildings that didn't snap
before do now!



New
We have added the following new buildings.
Wood
A half height wooden foundation.
Quarter Height wooden foundation
In large, and extra large varieties.
Extra large wood pillars as well.

Stone
New half height and quarter height foundations.
Also in very large varieties as well.
New wall side and upper pieces to go with the new gate corner pieces.
New stair inner and outer corner pieces
New stone curved railing 3


Changes Adjusted input/output height for machines. 
Building UI now scrolls instead of having pages 
Combined Steam power and water categories 
Harvesting from farm plots now drop satchels if inventory is full 


Bug Fixes
Fixed Basic Turrets not consuming ammo 
Fixed some Citadel and beacon 
UI not hiding mouse after closing 
Tentatively fixed toolbar lockup bug


Belts have had a ton of revisit and new features added. Introduced a new mode called Straight Mode where belts will automatically form in straight lines and turn 90 degrees. We also added the ability to hold CTRL to lock belts to a straight line. These also apply to Pipes and Rails.

notes.title: Orebound Update! Performance Gains, Balance, Features, UI upgrades and more!
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
Fellow Dwarves! Today we are pushing out a new version of Orebound to "thenextupdate" version of the game. If all goes well we intend to set this live for all players very soon, probably this week. 

So if you don't want to jump in early it wont be long until everyone gets this version! 

So what have we been doing over the last few weeks?! 

We have made a pretty extensive list of everything we have done below but we will start with some general news now.

We identified three major areas that have needed work over the last few months. 

1.  Performance on lower end machines. 
2.  Object count issues with the game causing it to crash.
3.  Saving and loading times. 

This update will mainly address problem #1 which is performance on lower end machines and it also touches on point three. Loading time. We have taken the time to invest in these areas to make sure the games future is going to be epic. Why is this? Our 2+ minute loading time was just too long for a new game. We also identified extremely long load times on larger games and we have made improvements here as well ( to come very soon in the next patch as well ).

The voxel world and generator needed a tonne of optimisation. We have spent many months here and now we are happy to say that we have reduced the initial game generation time down from 2+ minutes in some cases... To under 20 seconds. Yes that is correct. A new game and all its world contents can now be generated in under 20 seconds. For faster machines this might be under 10 seconds. 

The TLDR here is that we have worked incredibly hard to breakdown exactly how the game works and optimise it as much as possible. This will now in future allow us to add more and more layers to the game. 

Improved cave lighting and better deposit rendering.


We have spent a tonne of time improving how the game looks and feels underground. This includes allowing all the ores and the deposits to render correctly underground. We noticed that above ground ores would render fine but below ground they would not. This update fixes this so gems and gemlike materials now look very nice and shiney! 

We also gave caves a small make over to make them look nicer. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/7bde4e9430636316c9b272b66e90bf801bae4803.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/94630e66409a7eaeb494e9e374d04ca71f027803.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/cc00766ea1af6763c30ef103588c68c47cfa705d.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/bb07e3dc1fe97cde6284dfb442967306a4e8d32c.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/21d2d413df78eda59b63fa476fc1aaf5fe739632.png


Cave Updates and pickup items.

Caves can now spawn all sorts of pickups such as ores, gems and discarded loot bags from previous Dwarves long since gone. We are going to build on this in the future. But as you can see in this screenshot caves are now littered with items to find and pickup. We think this is going to be a great addition. 

As you might have noticed in the image above, caves will also now spawn more than 1 camp. Infact each cave and random from 1 to 5 camps to make it even more interesting! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/f0238224d4f085b7213265d78a28169285d964a0.png

Anvil Updates
Below is a sneak peak of all the cool features currently being worked on for the next major update for Orebound. We're going to be calling these Anvil Updates, They will contain major game feature additions and the first one will be announced very soon. You can find a preview of these new features in the Citadel now! 


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/10e5153afa3afd9d8b277aa8f63597f675dd65f0.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/5d2c56ba16cbb6994d70cad885c07e4a03807b79.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/1f10e4f0fc1167e9315f11057534ef10889c5f54.png

We have also done a full game balance and cost rework we think our fellow dwarves are going to enjoy it's a massive list so we will leave it below. 

There is even more in this update we have likely forgot, for example we nearly forgot to tell you the elevator is now faster and has a better noise. You'll noticed a tonne of changes and we might have missed some. Overall this is a pretty massive update and we hope you'll all enjoy it. 

We will leave the full list below for everyone to checkout and read and will be putting out an update about Anvil Update 1  soon! Thank you everyone! The Dwarven Devs

New
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png

When a building is destroyed, recipe in a machine is changed or a quest reward is given and items not able to be added to inventory and now placed in a loot bag next to the player to be picked up later
Added a warning message when mining ores with a full inventory.

Players will now drop a crate with items if their inventory is full. 

New UI improvements for the Navigator. this will now show users they can place drills on deposits. Also improved navigator UI in general. Pretty much an entire overhaul. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/b819fff5812d6e241193b57aef4715abfc52aa79.png


Changes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/9220a5f331cf8099242a123c842334ef040c4a54.png



 Better Pickaxes now give more loot (iron gives x2, Electrum gives x3)
 Auto smelter now requires 1 dust per ingot rather than 2
 Boulders now give more stone when destroyed
 Rebalanced turret damage so kinetic and flame turrets do more damage than the mini turrets
 All machines now have 500 health
 Allow overlap building option is now available for machines as well
 Constructor now makes items at double the speed of the blacksmith
 Barrelling alcohol now takes less time
 Can no longer drink barrels
 Changed lava damaged at bottom of world from 2 to 10
 Changed farm 2 research icon
 Empty hotbar slots can now be highlighted
Infinite deposits no longer mineable with pickaxe to prevent rapid game progression. 





Bug Fixes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png


 Fixed Gem Infuser being able to craft multiple Thandor gems if destroyed and replaced
 Fixed some stumps sometimes not being harvestable
 Changed large wood foundation collision so you can now go under it
 Changed collision on world borders to stop buildings being placed outside it
 Adjusted collision on large ore vein to be more fitting on model
 Fixed goblins having a 90% chance to fight an ally when hit by them (now correct 10%)
 Fixed bug with tunnels not spawning that should have been.
 The new larger caves now have upto 5 goblin camps and other points of interest.  They will spawn anywhere between 1 and 5
 Increased boar spawning on surface.
 Fixed a russian mistranslation of "Chest" meaning (in Russian) human pectorals, to chest (a storage unit)
 Fixed Restoring health when eating herbed boar
 Can now walk through wooden pillar gaps
 Fire effect from flame traps and lava level no longer continue after death
 Fixed trap collision issues
 Map select image now only changes if new image is different
 Fixed mines not doing any damage
 Fixed death chest being destroyed by enemies
 Updated King's market dwarf's clothes
 Fixed some traps affecting npc navigation
 Recipe tooltips now show crafting time with machine efficiency multiplier applied
 Fixed Flame turret not taking damage
 Fixed boar cooking sound SFX not being effected by SFX volume
 Fixed broken explosives quest


Full game balance rework
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
We have been listening to you & decided to rework the core design of Orebound in a way that improves freedom and the general flow of gameplay. For the most part everything has been made cheaper and more accessible with a handful of cost increases here and there.
The following is the new balance changes.

Research station changes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png

Factory and automation:

  Automation 1  kept at 500 gold.
  Automation 2  reduced  from 2500 gold and 25 iron ingots to 1500 gold and 10 iron ingots.
 Automation 3  reduced  from 5000 gold, 25 iron cogs & 25 iron plates to 3000 gold and 20 iron plates.
 Automation 4 reduced  from 75,000 gold and 100 copper ingots to 50,000 gold and 50 copper pipe-works
 Automation 5 reduced from 250,000 gold, 100 silver dinnerware and 100 gold bracers to 200,000 gold, 75 silver dinnerware and 75 gold bracers.
 Automation 6 unchanged
 Automation 7 reduced from 10 million gold, 100 ruby, 100 sapphire and 100 emerald ingots to 5 million gold with 100 of each gemstone ingot.
 With so much new content being added to the game (and even more on the way) we realised how difficult it was to explore all aspects of gameplay in the early tiers of the game when the player has less access to gold.
 These changes have been made to help get the early game flowing quicker into automation while also reducing the grind factor of the later tiers to help improve the feel of the game.

 
 
Dwarves vaults:

 Tier 1  reduced from 1,000 gold to 500 gold
 Tier 2 reduced from 5,000 gold to 2,000 gold
 Previous tiers 3 & 4 have been merged into one, bringing the auto-market and grand coin storage into the same tier priced at 15,000 gold
 These changes aim to help the player manage their gold far easier in the early game stages.



Crafting

 Tier 2 reduced from 5,000 gold to 2,500 gold
 Tier 3 reduced from 20,000 gold to 10,000 gold
 Considering the upgrade station requires resources to upgrade it as well as the initial research requirements, we wanted to make it easier for players to explore the tools and weapon variety’s we have in game.

 
Navigator
·       Copper tier reduced from 2,500 to 750 gold
·       Gold and silver reduced from 15,000 to 5,000 gold
·       Gemstones reduced from 30,000 to 15,000 gold
Copper was far too highly priced for the early stages of the game and for a game about digging, we want to make it as easy as possible to find the treasures of the world!
 
Food & farming
·       Tier 1 kept at 500 gold
·       Tier 2 reduced from 1,500 to 1,000 gold
·       Tier 3 reduced from 5,000 to 3,000 gold
·       Previous tier’s 4 and 5 have been merged into one, costing 10,000 gold.
 
With food being a vital part of survival now, it was important to make it accessible to the early stages of gameplay. We also decided to merge the potion & automated farming stages into one.
 
Base building
·       Tier 1 reduced from 2,500 gold to 500 gold
·       Tier 2 reduced from  5,000 gold to 1,000 gold
·       Tier 3 reduced from 7,500 gold to 2,000 gold
·       Tiers 4 and 5 have been merged into one costing 3,000 gold Base building was unjustly expensive for the player to gain access to. It is now far cheaper to allow for a much more unrestricted fortress building experience!

Explosives
·       Tier 2 reduced from 10,000 to 5,000 gold
·       Tier 3 reduced from 50,000 to 25,000 gold
The barrier of entry to explosives was previously a bit too high and this has been reduced now.
 
Transport
·       Tier 1 reduced from 2,000 to 1,000 gold
·       Tier 2 reduced from 7,500 to 5,000 gold
Keeping with the general theme of allowing easier access to gameplay aspects, we reduced the costs of transportation too
 
Defences
·       Tier 1 reduced from 1,000 to 500 gold
·       Tier 2 reduced from 5,000 to 2,500 gold
·       Tier 3 reduced from 15,000 to 7,500 gold
·       Tier 4 reduced from 30,0000 to 15,000 gold
Turrets and traps are a great feature of the game and we want players to be able to line their base with them more easily.
 
 
Building cost reworks
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/fb09facc9030dea66344944703d696ca1f9655f2.png
In line with the research station changes, we have also rebalanced every single placeable building recipe. This has been done to create a smoother transition from early to late game and improve the general feeling of the game.
 
Crafting
·       Kings Questboard reduced from 25 stone & 25 wood to 15 stone & 15 wood
·       Tool station reduced from 25 stone & 25 wood to 20 stone & 20 wood.
·       Research station reduced from 20 stone, 20 wood and 20 iron ore to 20 stone, 20 wood and 10 iron ore.
·       Manual smelter reduced from 50 stone and 10 coal to 30 stone & 10 coal.
·       Blacksmith reduced from 25 iron ingots and 20 wood to 15 iron ingots and 20 wood.
·       Kings market reduced from 60 wood and 40 iron ore to 40 wood and 10 iron ore.
 
These changes will help the early game and onboarding process feel less resource demanding & improve the general feel of gameplay.
 
Machines Reductions
·       Belt drill reduced from 10 iron plates, 15 iron plates and 15 iron cogs to 10 iron plates, 10 copper plates and 10 iron cogs
·       Auto crusher reduced from 40 wood, 10 iron plates and 15 cogs to 30 wood, 10 iron plates, 10 iron cogs
·       Smelter reduced from 20 iron plates, 20 copper plates, 10 iron cogs and 20 coal to 15 iron plates, 15 copper plates, 5 iron cogs and 5 copper pipes

notes.title: Quality Of Life Update
notes.notes:
Fellow Dwarves!  ⛏️  Yesterday we set the next update live onto the main games branch. Quite a few things in there and It’s now live to all players. I'll list them below! 

New features

Herbs have been added as a growable to farm plots

Herb seeds can be gotten with a random chance from herb bushes.

Key input rebinding has been changed to be less of a hassle.  This was an issue for some.  If a key is already bound, you'll be asked to confirm setting that key and it will remove the already bound key from its binding.

Added a progress bar in the Machine UI to display crafting progress

Changes


Due to new dwarves STILL struggling to find the relay in the citadel, it has been moved to be closer to your bedroom.

Improvements to AI inside of the tutorial map to stop them getting stuck on each other.

Boar spawning has been increased by 20%

Fixed snap points of new tiles on stone foundation and square stone pieces.

Changed crafting recipe for navigator from ruby ingots to ruby ore

The player now has a few cooked boar meat when they start

Different alcohols now give different inebrations.

Altered vsync checkbox size in settings.

Instructions in toolbar now update keybinds displayed

One of the tutorial quests no longer consumes an item on completion

Typo fix up on tool stations

Typo fix up on quests (English only)
 
Bug fixes

You should now not be able to complete a quest unless you have the necessary inventory space.

Blacksmith returns contents when destroyed.

Fixed a small bug that wasn't allowing items to be shift clicked into the Minecart Station

Fixed a bug where you could stack items of 1 stack max (Tools)

Fixed cost consumption and refund for long belts

Please let us know if you have any questions or issues. 

The future 

We want to take a moment to discuss Orebound and what we are currently working on for the end of the month.  🔧 

Adjusted plans slightly based on player feedback

We are delaying the new map and will pick a new date for that in the near future. We got very excited about adding a new map to play that was custom made, however after hearing the community we feel there's more important things to come first.  We are still working on this bespoke experience and it will be great when it’s done. 

So what are we doing?  🤔  Well we’ve read your feedback, read all the reviews ( literally all of them ), watched gameplay and seen what still needs to be done. 

Quality of life is one of the biggest areas that need improvement, so we’ve pushed that forward, after that we are also working on how our factory system works. We understand how slick and polished this needs to be. So many people want stands for belts, want the ability to snap belts in lines, and have more functionality to make a base without  frustration. Improvements to splitters and snaps for factories etc. We think there's a lot here that will make everyone's experience better and we want this to happen now so it’s all done for the future. 

The key rebind system also needed an overhaul which is in this version of the game now. We set up the keybind system when we didnt have many keys in the game. As this grew it caused issues. So this needed a work ( currently in this update.  )

We have noticed some players are turning on and off build systems without knowing it. Causing frustrations. Orebound contains an extremely powerful build system so it’s important we make sure that the quality of life for these tools is really good. Something we want to work on in January and February. 

So we have decided to work on that for the next few weeks but this is also alongside two other major things.

We have made some huge improvements to performance and massive factories with a new asynchronous system for belt items. This basically means you will be able to have thousands of items on belts without a CPU slow down. Something that is a big pain point for some people and something everyone will encounter eventually with a mega base. This will be a massive improvement.

We have also made changes to how items are registered inside inventories and storage. Our inventory system, for example how we detect things going in and out at scale, was inefficient and caused performance issues. Again this will be another massive improvement.

We hope rolling all of this out will ease up on CPU usage for the game for the factory side of things and essentially mean you can build anything without major performance loss.  💪 

We will demonstrate these soon after we are done testing them. 

There are two other areas we need to improve on. One is the navigation and the other is the voxel landscape. Both are quite CPU intensive; these are the next areas we want to focus on ( in terms of optimisation ) to make the game even better in the future. These are more long term. 

We are also ever closer to putting our GAS system live for the RPG aspect of the player. @deathwyrm has done some great work here and it’s going to allow our RPG game to go up multiple tiers of quality. 

We plan to roll out as much as we can for the end of January 2025 and keep working of course releasing more updates throughout the year. 

All of these additions will build a solid foundation for Orebounds development over 2025 and we cant wait to bring you more awesome updates! 

Thank you fellow Dwarves for your continued support! Please remember to drop us a review if you’re enjoying the game. We’re a small team and it really helps us out! 🙏

notes.title: UPDATE 3 - Farming, Crafting and building Update!
notes.notes:
Fellow Dwarves! We hope you’re doing great! Tonight we are putting the Food and Farming update live! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/db36c78b29a94ac25420e5775ef7e1e0b51766d8.png

This update is quite a large one so it’s taken us just over 5 weeks. We want to explain why!

Starting off with some annoying news. We have had to postpone the Brewking and the Orge map release that was scheduled for today. We have made great progress here but we need to do more and we’re not quite happy with the quality. The Brewking and the Ogre map is a custom bespoke map with its own quests and it’s taking slightly longer than expected. We have rescheduled this for the next major update in January 2025. We’re sorry for doing this to our fellow dwarves however we were not satisfied with the quality and we already had much to do. However, here's a sneak peak of the level. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/9d144de088581c71ccfa445c83906f73ef97df49.png

Everything else from here is good news! 

After the launch of Orebound we identified some of the larger issues that were in the game. This being optimisation, bugs, crashes, navigation issues etc. We rapidly got to work fixing these issues and put out hotfixes and two large updates to help with these things. 

Some of the bugs were deeper than we initially thought. Be it on older pc’s lower end CPU’s and the likes. 

We knew when we set out to make Orebound we would need to try and push some limits or we would end up being just another factory game. 

This is not where we wanted to be because although this probably would have led us to short term success it wouldn't be a long term impactful change to the genre that would be interesting and expandable over the longer term. 

What we have been doing over the last month is watching, listening, gathering feedback from the community and from refund notes ( this is a horrible place ). When we launched we knew our roadmap would change with feedback. 

We didn't initially want to put a roadmap out because we agreed that when thousands of players hit the game that would just burn the map because we would listen to that feedback and change it anyway.

What we’ve learned since launch is that you all want more in all areas, which is great and that’s what we intend to do. However some areas need more work than others, totally understandable and we wanted to get a decent approach on this. 

What we initially set out to do was to work on all areas at the same time and bring the game up at an even pace. However we have actually changed how we are going to approach this. 

What we are now going to do is focus all our energies into one or a few places at one time. So going forward that’s likely what you’ll see in our update patterns. 

What this means now is that we are going to make a roadmap that focuses on specific areas for the game and release those accordingly. We’re hoping to have something to show you all in Jan 2025 on the exact development trajectory for Orebound! 

All that being said, we have a lot to share today! 


Technology

In the back end, we have part integrated the unreal engine Gameplay Ability System for hunger and inebriation. GAS is incredibly powerful with it's abilities, effects and modification system which is going to allow us to do a lot in the future. We visualise different food giving different buffs to speed, health regenerations and a whole host of other possibilities we are fleshing out. It also comes out the box with multiplayer support and replication, saving us a ton of time with what we'd have to test with our old current system that is being phased out. We are still in the process of integration, but it's such a big technological change that it's worth being mentioned.

We have also been implementing and improving a full quest system and quest tracking system into the game. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/b269ec590aa48a580d42c07499acb5a6ae92ff6a.png

Farming! 

New farming system with placeable farm plots in small, large, small with earthstones and large with earthstones.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/5884d811d7460d2c3c0f67e3fdd1c730445791f4.png

A new hunger mechanic with 4 hunger states. Starving, hungry, satiated and well fed.

During starving, you will take continual damage until dead or hunger is restored.

When satiated, health will regenerate by a small amount.

When well fed, health regenerates at double the well satiated rate.

When dieing, 35 hunger will be restored every time.

Hops and barely is now split, into hops, and barley, and growable on the farm plots.

Changes to the icon for the hops and barley instead of that wheat icon.

New growable, berries and its seed.

New growable, mushrooms and mushroom spores.


Brewing! 

He have also introduced brewcraft to the game. This will allow players to brew ales and whiskeys and have a fun time! You'll be able to restore health and hunger, but there might be some side effects...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/ecc74f53cc941a738c517108493f69c8c9d05eb7.png

New Building Pieces

Bug fixes.

Some of these are for the previous 0.0.0.50d patch

Some input control fixes.

Fixes for orc weapon offsets

Switching hotbar forces end of blocking

Back end boar spam when failing to find a path should stop

Fixed bug when cave foliage wasn't spawning

Fixed player not being at save location

Custom Foliage

We are starting to add more fully custom foliage to the game to add more variety to the world.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45150706/4436be42623b67e66668781971da4ea168603804.png

 Tutorial Level 

Orebound is a huge and complex game, we have received many requests for a tutorial so here it is!

We’ve added a new map in which a new player can exclusively learn the core basics of Orebound through a series of quests. This was one of the highest request things from new players. Now you can practice -Collecting basic resources -Making tools using the crafting bench -Using the Ore Navigator to search and mine for resources within the Voxel world -Unlocking new tiers in the Research station -Smelting ingots & using them to craft items in the blacksmith -Making use of the Kings Market to earn money -How to place the portable drill for early-tier automation -Making use of wild plants to make food -Hunting boars and how to get food out of them -Mining automation with a large belt fed drill -learning about steam power with water pumps and boilers -Basics of in game combat -Practice fighting goblins -Achievements for completing the new level

Changes / Fixed
Performance optimizations for the Factory side of the game. Players should notice better performance on large factories.

Fixes and polish to various UI.

More work on factory optimizations, including more performant and efficient ways to render belts and their items, as well as better backend handling of inventories and the entire factory backend process.

Soon we will release an in depth update road map of what our plan is for Orebound. Also we hear you. You all want multiplayer! 

We shall keep hammering the anvil!

The Dwarven Developers.
